name: File eManifests and clear cross-border loads
summary: Every truck entering Canada or the US must send the border agency an electronic manifest describing the trip and its shipments before it arrives: at least an hour ahead, or 30 minutes for FAST trips into the US. The carrier's customs coordinators gather the invoice and broker details, enter the shipments with their PARS or PAPS numbers and the driver, tractor and trailer details, transmit, fix rejects, and send the numbers to each importer's customs broker, who files the release. They check the release is on file before the truck arrives and help when it is referred at the port. Missing invoices, vague commodity descriptions, wrong plates, late driver or trailer changes and brokers who have not filed are the common causes of border delays.

baseline.org_archetype: A Canadian LTL and truckload carrier of about 3,000 employees whose truckload division runs about 400 company sleeper tractors and 380 owner-operators within Canada and across the US border, on a carrier TMS with EDI, ELDs and an eManifest service provider.
baseline.notes: Customs desk of 14 coordinators covering 24 hours a day, filing about 3,000 crossings a month (mostly truckload, some LTL linehaul exchanges) through an eManifest service provider.

trigger: A cross-border truckload trip is assigned to a driver, or an LTL linehaul trailer for a US exchange is built.
end_state: The truck is released at the port and the crossing is closed in the TMS, or the load is held and passed to the border-hold process.

volume.seasonality: Follows truckload volume; lower in spring 2020 when US-Canada trade dropped, higher in the autumn peak.

evidence.note: Taken from the org file's border-crossings demand driver (about 35% of truckload loads plus linehaul exchanges with US partners).

surge.cause: Border disruption (bridge blockade, system outage or flood closure)

evidence.note: Copied from the org file's process map entry: events such as the February 2022 Ambassador Bridge blockade and the November 2021 British Columbia floods, when trips were re-routed and manifests amended. Sizes are the author's estimate.
Most of the 14 coordinators' time; the rest goes to border holds (about 90 a month) and broker queries.
Small share of driver managers' time briefing drivers on border paperwork.

systems.name: Transportation management system (LTL and truckload operations, billing, rating)
eManifest service provider (CBSA ACI and US CBP ACE)
Document imaging for bills of lading and delivery receipts
Email, phone system and contact centre software
Electronic logging devices and telematics platform

steps.name: Cross-border trip enters the customs queue
steps.description: When a planner flags a truckload trip as cross-border, or an LTL linehaul trailer is built for a US partner exchange, the TMS adds it to the customs desk queue with the shipments, the planned port of entry and the ETA at the border.

evidence.note: Common carrier practice; author's description.

steps.name: Gather the shipment documents
steps.description: The customs coordinator opens the crossing, pulls the bill of lading and commercial invoice from the imaging system or the shipper's email, and checks that the importer's customs broker is named on the order.

error.defect_description: Old invoice or wrong broker picked up.

next.condition: LTL linehaul trailer with many freight bills

evidence.note: Share of loads with missing documents is the author's estimate; LTL share follows the org file's trigger from freight bill entry.

steps.name: Ask the shipper for the invoice or broker
steps.description: The coordinator emails or calls the shipper for the commercial invoice, the importer of record or the broker's name, explaining that the truck cannot cross without them.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Shipper sends the missing documents
steps.description: The shipper's office emails the invoice or names the broker. Small shippers and shipments picked up late in the day often answer only the next morning.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Build the shipment record with its PARS or PAPS number
steps.description: The coordinator takes the next PARS (into Canada) or PAPS (into the US) number from the carrier's pre-printed barcode range and enters the shipment in the eManifest service provider's software: shipper, consignee, commodity description, quantity, weight and port of entry, copying details from the TMS order.

error.defect_description: Typing error or a vague commodity description such as 'general merchandise'.

evidence.note: Data elements and the PARS release link from the CBSA; minutes are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Build one shipment record per freight bill
steps.description: For an LTL linehaul trailer the coordinator enters a shipment record for each freight bill on the trailer, often 10 to 30, each with its own PARS or PAPS number, consignee, description and weight, and checks that every bill has a broker.

error.defect_description: A bill left off the manifest or given the wrong broker.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Check commodity descriptions and data
steps.description: The coordinator reads each description against the CBSA's guidance on detailed commodity descriptions and the invoice, replaces vague terms with what the goods are, and checks quantities and weights against the bill of lading.

error.defect_description: A vague description slips through and draws a penalty or a referral.

control.basis: CBSA Advance Commercial Information (ACI eManifest): cargo and conveyance data at least 1 hour before arrival, accurate and complete, AMPS penalties for late or wrong data; CBP ACE eManifest under 19 CFR 123.92 (1 hour, 30 minutes for FAST)

evidence.note: The CBSA requires clear cargo descriptions and lists unclear descriptions among penalized errors; minutes are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Enter the trip data: driver, tractor, trailer and seals
steps.description: The coordinator creates the trip (conveyance) record with the driver's name, date of birth, citizenship and FAST card number, the tractor and trailer plates and their province or state, seal numbers, port of entry and ETA, and links the shipment records to it.

control.basis: CBSA Advance Commercial Information (ACI eManifest): cargo and conveyance data at least 1 hour before arrival, accurate and complete, AMPS penalties for late or wrong data; CBP ACE eManifest under 19 CFR 123.92 (1 hour, 30 minutes for FAST)

evidence.note: Timing rules from the CBSA page and 19 CFR 123.92: at least 1 hour before arrival, 30 minutes for FAST trips into the US; valid plates required. Minutes are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Transmit the eManifest and read the response
steps.description: The service provider sends the trip and shipments to the CBSA (ACI) or CBP (ACE) and returns an acceptance or a reject with an error code within minutes; accepted trips show in the portal with their status.

evidence.note: 99.2% to 99.7% of highway pre-arrival data was sent electronically in 2019-2022; the reject share is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Fix a rejected eManifest
steps.description: The coordinator reads the reject code, corrects the plate format, carrier code, duplicate cargo control number or missing field, and resends.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Send PARS or PAPS numbers and documents to the broker
steps.description: The coordinator emails or faxes the commercial invoice and bill of lading to each importer's customs broker with the PARS or PAPS number, so the broker can file the release request against the same cargo control number.

error.defect_description: Documents sent to the wrong broker.

evidence.note: Brokers file the release request (PARS) or entry (PAPS) linked by the cargo control number; minutes are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Broker files the release request or entry
steps.description: The importer's customs broker files the PARS release request with the CBSA or the PAPS entry with CBP, using the invoice and the carrier's number. Brokers work through a queue and file late-day shipments in the evening or next morning.

evidence.note: Release requests can be filed up to 45 days before arrival; broker turnaround is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Check that the release is on file
steps.description: Before the truck nears the border the coordinator checks the portal notices for each shipment: a PARS release recommendation or referral from the CBSA, or the PAPS entry on file with CBP. Missing ones are chased.

error.defect_description: Shipment shown as on file when only the manifest is.

next.condition: release on file for every shipment

evidence.note: For release requests sent at least an hour before arrival, a recommendation was ready on arrival in 99.4% of cases; the share needing a chase is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Chase the broker
steps.description: The coordinator phones or emails the broker to find out why the release is not on file, resends documents or obtains a missing importer number, and, if the truck is close, tells the driver manager to slow or hold the driver.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Confirm border paperwork with the driver
steps.description: The driver manager sends the driver the eManifest trip number and checks that the driver has the PARS or PAPS labels, invoices and seal, and that the truck, trailer and port have not changed since filing.

error.defect_description: Driver sets off without the invoice or labels.

next.condition: driver, trailer, port or ETA changed

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Amend the eManifest after a change
steps.description: When the driver, tractor, trailer or port changes after filing, the coordinator amends the trip in the portal and retransmits before the truck reaches the border, because the driver cannot use a different port without an update.

error.defect_description: Amendment sent too late, so the truck arrives with stale data.

control.basis: CBSA Advance Commercial Information (ACI eManifest): cargo and conveyance data at least 1 hour before arrival, accurate and complete, AMPS penalties for late or wrong data; CBP ACE eManifest under 19 CFR 123.92 (1 hour, 30 minutes for FAST)

evidence.note: Corrections, including a change of port, must be sent as soon as known; minutes are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Truck reaches the border and clears primary inspection
steps.description: The truck drives to the port, queues and stops at the primary booth, where the officer scans the manifest and release and releases the truck or refers it inside.

evidence.note: About 9% of highway crossings into Canada are referred from primary (7% to 13% by year); inspection takes one to two minutes. The wait is the drive from the planning point to the border plus the queue, author's estimate.

steps.name: Support a referral at the port
steps.description: The coordinator takes the driver's call from the counter, finds what is missing or wrong, gets the broker to file or correct the release, and sends corrected data; selected loads are examined and some are held.

evidence.note: Goods without a release request cannot be released at the first port and are held or moved in-bond; hold share is the author's estimate, giving about 80 holds a month against about 90 border holds in the org file.

steps.name: Confirm the release and close the crossing
steps.description: The coordinator sees the release or arrival notice in the portal, marks the crossing cleared in the TMS so tracing and billing show it, and files the manifest record.

error.defect_description: Crossing not closed, so the trip shows as stuck at the border.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

exceptions.name: Missing invoice or broker
exceptions.description: The shipper has not sent the commercial invoice or named the broker; the coordinator chases it, sometimes overnight.

exceptions.name: eManifest rejected
exceptions.description: The CBSA or CBP rejects the transmission for a plate format, carrier code or duplicate number error, and it is fixed and resent.

exceptions.name: Release not on file
exceptions.description: The broker has not filed the release or entry when the truck nears the border; the coordinator chases and may hold the driver short of the port.

exceptions.name: Change after filing
exceptions.description: A driver swap, trailer change, new port or new ETA forces an amendment before arrival.

exceptions.name: Referral or hold at the port
exceptions.description: The officer refers the truck inside; most are released after the broker fixes the release, and about three in ten are held for examination or a missing release.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from the crossing entering the customs queue to release at the port

evidence.note: Author's estimate: crossings are flagged when the trip is planned, usually the day before the truck reaches the border, and most of the elapsed time is the truck driving to the port.

benchmarks.unit: share of highway crossings referred from primary inspection

evidence.note: Evaluation of eManifest, table 6.

benchmarks.unit: share of release requests filed at least 1 hour before arrival with a recommendation ready on arrival

evidence.note: Evaluation of eManifest.

pain_points.description: Shipment details are re-keyed from the TMS order and the invoice into the eManifest software, which costs time and produces plate, weight and description errors.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; many carriers' TMS were linked to their eManifest provider by 2019, but smaller links and LTL bills were still keyed.

pain_points.description: The carrier depends on brokers it does not choose; trucks wait when a broker has not filed the release.

evidence.note: Without a release request the goods cannot be released at the first port.

pain_points.description: Missing commercial invoices from shippers hold up filing, often overnight.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

pain_points.description: Late changes of driver, trailer or port need amendments; a missed amendment means a referral or a penalty.

evidence.note: Changes must be sent as soon as known; drivers cannot switch ports without an update; AMPS penalties for incorrect data.

assumptions: One case is one loaded border crossing in either direction; trucks entering the US file ACE and trucks entering Canada file ACI, through the same eManifest service provider, so the steps are shown once.
About 12% of crossings are LTL linehaul trailers with many freight bills, which take much longer to manifest (s06).
The org file lists the customs broker's customs_release as a trigger; in practice it is a response within the case (s12-s13) rather than what starts it, so it is not a trigger here.
Held loads end this process with the outcome 'border_hold' and pass to tl-border-holds; the org file links border holds only from the CBSA and CBP.

Staffing check: coordinator touch time averages about 35 minutes per crossing, which at 3,000 crossings implies about 13 FTE at 130 productive hours a month, against 14 coordinators who also work border holds and cover 24 hours a day; the desk has little slack.
Loaded costs come from the org file.

sources.title: Highway mode: Transmit electronic commercial data (Advance Commercial Information / eManifest)
sources.supports: Highway carriers transmit cargo and conveyance data at least 1 hour before arrival at the port of entry; corrections must be sent as soon as known, including a change of port; tractor and trailer plates must be valid and cargo descriptions clear; late, incorrect or incomplete data can draw AMPS monetary penalties; contingency plan for system outages.

sources.title: Memorandum D17-1-4: Release of Commercial Goods
sources.supports: Importers or brokers may submit PARS release requests electronically up to 45 days before arrival; a border services officer reviews them and records a release or refer recommendation; the cargo control number links release and cargo documents; on arrival release or refer notices go to the broker; without a release request the goods cannot be released at the first port and are held or moved in-bond to a sufferance warehouse.

sources.title: 19 CFR 123.92
sources.publisher: Legal Information Institute, Cornell Law School
sources.supports: The incoming truck carrier must transmit advance electronic cargo information so that CBP receives it no later than 30 minutes or 1 hour before the truck reaches the first US port of arrival, depending on the CBP-approved system; under the dual-party option the importer or its broker may send part of it.

sources.title: Trucks Must Give One-Hour Notice Unless They're FAST
sources.supports: Inbound trucks to the US must give electronic notice one hour before reaching the border, FAST-registered trucks 30 minutes.

sources.title: Evaluation of eManifest, Final Report
sources.publisher: Canada Border Services Agency, Program Evaluation Division
sources.supports: Highway pre-arrival transmissions of about 14 million (2019-20) to 16 million (2021-22) a year; electronic submission 99.2% to 99.7%; referrals from primary inspection to the counter 13% (2018-19), 10% (2019-20), 8% (2020-21), 7% (2021-22), about 9% on average; a release recommendation was available on arrival for 99.4% of release requests sent at least one hour before arrival.

sources.title: Documenting and Determining Distributions, Trends, and Relations in Truck Lanes at International Border Crossing Facilities
sources.supports: 1,085 truck crossings at the Ambassador Bridge in June 2014: crossing time always higher for trucks entering the US, peaks near 8 a.m. and 5 p.m., crossings concentrated Tuesday to Thursday; 19 of 1,085 trucks (1.75%) sent to secondary inspection; inspections generally 1 to 2 minutes.
